title: Event-driven surge shield and slipstream scaler
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Goal: design and prototype a new autoscaling policy engine variant (Slipstream Scaler) that combines event-driven surge detection with a conservative (shielded) scaling layer to maintain throughput guarantees for Dedicated capacity while bounding cost and preserving SLOs. The policy will be pluggable in the policy-compiler and aim to reduce both underprovisioning during spikes and overshoot during noisy load.

Background: Current scaling controllers oscillate on bursty token-level traffic and sometimes overcommit GPU pools to absorb transient peaks, increasing cost for customers on Dedicated plans. We need a controller that: (1) recognizes short-lived request surges and defers large-scale allocation when acceptable, (2) uses predictive slipstreaming for long tails to pre-warm capacity safely, and (3) exposes clear safety limits and observable signals for operations.

What this ticket contains: design doc summary, target signals, algorithm pseudocode, safety limit matrix, experiment plan, rollout plan, and acceptance criteria. This is intended to be an engineering-first RFC with measurable simulation results and a reference implementation as a feature flag in the autoscale service.
target_metrics: Primary metrics used by the policy: token_throughput_per_tenant (tokens/s), request_concurrency, p95_latency_generation_ms, queue_depth, eviction_rate_kv_cache. Secondary metrics for safety: observed_slew_rate(percent_capacity/min), node_utilization_gpu, preemptible_eviction_count. The controller will compute a weighted composite target: target_throughput = max(tenant_commit_throughput, observed_rolling_quantile(0.90) * margin_factor).
algorithm_overview: 1) Event detector: short-window (30s) and medium-window (5m) detectors compute arrival-rate deltas and burst_score. 2) Surge shield layer: if burst_score > transient_threshold && predicted_spike_duration < transient_horizon then apply 'shield' — temporary local queuing and rate-limited admission with token-bucket on request ingress. Do not allocate capacity for spikes shorter than transient_horizon. 3) Slipstream predictor: for persistent increases (detected on 3 consecutive medium windows or by an exponential-weighted moving average), compute required capacity using a conservative projection (alpha factor) and pre-warm up to prewarm_limit in staggered steps (slipstream steps). 4) Safety layer: enforce min/max instance bounds, max_slew_rate, per-tenant headroom reserve, and isolate tenant surges using tenant_fencing so they cannot steal shared buffers beyond defined credit. 5) Fallback: if latency SLOs would be breached due to withholding scale, automatically fallback to short-lived cold-capacity pools or model-variant downgrades per routing policy.
safety_limits_spec: Config knobs and default suggested values (subject to tuning): max_slew_rate=10%_capacity_per_minute, min_headroom_per_tenant=5%_capacity_or_committed_throughput, transient_horizon=45s, transient_threshold=burst_score>3, slipstream_alpha=1.25 (scale by 25% over projected need), prewarm_limit=30%_fleet_capacity_per_zone, stagger_step_seconds=30, cooldown_window=300s, emergency_backstop_enabled=true. All values must be configurable via policy DSL with per-tenant override. Any change to emergency_backstop or max_slew_rate requires an ops review and release note.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulation: in historical-sim replay for three representative tenants (low-burst, bursty short spikes, heavy diurnal growth), slipstream scaler reduces overprovisioning cost by >=18% vs current stepper while keeping p95_generation_latency <= existing baseline + 8%. 2) Canary: gated rollout on 5% of Dedicated fleets, no escalation incidents for 48h, and monitored metrics show no regression in request success rate or eviction anomalies. 3) Observability: new dashboard panels for burst_score, projected_prewarms, active_shield_count, and per-tenant headroom breaches. 4) Rollback: feature toggle allows instant revert to prior controller with state reconciliation within 2 minutes.
design_tradeoffs:
- Conservative pre-warm (slipstream_alpha > 1) reduces SLO risk but increases cost; simulations will find Pareto point.
- Shielding short spikes avoids churn and cost but may degrade tail latency briefly; to mitigate we provide fast local queueing and prioritized short-lived burst pools.
- Tenant fencing prevents noisy neighbors but complicates bin-packing; we'll introduce soft limits first with telemetry before hard isolation.
- Predictive models add complexity; initial implementation will use simple EWMA + windowed quantiles and will evolve to ML predictors if justified.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement event detector and surge shield in autoscale-svc with feature flag; simulation harness to replay traces. Phase 2 (2 weeks): add slipstream predictor, safety limit enforcer, and config DSL. Phase 3 (1 week): integrate observability panels and rollout canary. Phase 4 (1 week): iterate on knobs from canary feedback and prepare docs. Phase 5: gradual rollout across Dedicated clusters with automated rollback policy. Unit tests + integration tests + chaos tests to validate cooldowns and rollback semantics.
experiment_plan: - Historical replay: run against last 90 days of request traces for 3 tenant archetypes. - A/B canary: 5% fleets for 7 days vs control. - Failure injection: simulate node preemption and KV cache eviction to validate fallback. Key success metrics: cost_delta, p95_latency_delta, scale_count_variance, false_positive_shield_rate.
observability_and_alerting: New metrics emitted: autoscale.surge_shield.active, autoscale.slipstream.prewarms, autoscale.safety.headroom_breach, autoscale.slew_rate.current. Alerts: headroom_breach_rate > 1% for 10m => paged, unexpected_prewarm_failure => page, fallback_activation_rate > 0.1% sustained => investigate. Dashboards: per-tenant heatmap of shield hits and prewarm events.
rollout_and_fallback: Start in 'adaptive' feature flag (off by default). Canary to dedicated-aria-zone-1 at 5% fleets. Observability gates enforced before expanding. Fallback mechanisms: instant feature-flag off, emergency_backstop that allocates cold-capacity up to 10% of fleet to absorb immediate spikes, automatic revert to alternating stepper-controller if backoff thresholds triggered three times in 10 minutes.
